thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired — PD#PDR12345 — hosted-api-us-west-2 error-rate > 1.5% (5xx) in 1m window. Trigger: synthetic-canary-errors. https://pd/redwood/PDR12345

maya: pinging oncall, saw a spike in 5xx right after the canary rollout started. might be noisy but wanted to flag.

simon: i'm on it, grabbing ingress + backend logs now. maya can you stop canary traffic to reduce noise?

maya: removing canary routing in 1... `kubectl patch svc hosted-api -p '{"spec": {"selector": {"canary":"false"}}}'` — on it.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: alert auto-resolved — PD#PDR12345 cleared (threshold dropped).

eli: saw the auto-resolve, pd re-fired ~30s later though. looks like a flappy metric: canary probes oscillating between healthy/unhealthy and tripping the rule.

maya: ok thinking rollback of canary if it keeps flapping. want to verify it's not a backend regression first.

simon: ingress logs show a high rate of `503` with `upstream reset` from a small subset of backends. hypothesis: canary burst exhausted per-host conn limits -> upstream resets. increasing proxy max connections for that route to validate.

maya: applied envoy patch to canary route: `max_connections: 200` and restarted the envoy deployment for canary workers.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: alert fired again — PD#PDR46 (same metric). auto-resolve cycles detected.

simon: i'm going to add a temporary silence for the alert rule (5m) while we validate the envoy change, to avoid repeated PD noise.

oncall-lead: +1 to silence, please add a short writeup so SRE knows why we muted alerts.

maya: silenced via `/pd silence --service hosted-api --duration 5m --note "suspected canary conn exhaustion"` — added note.

eli: quick customer-impact check: no increase in real-user 5xx (RUM/edge metrics show stable p50/p95), only canary origin IPs showing elevated errors. looks internal.

simon: confirmed, traffic analysis -> source IPs tied to canary labels. backend warms up a bit slowly causing retries to fail; will add a short retry policy on the canary path to smooth transient failures.

maya: added retry policy: `retries: 2, per_try_timeout: 1s` for the canary route and lowered canary traffic rate from 5% to 1%.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD#PDR46 auto-resolved (silence active).

oncall-lead: thanks team. we should keep monitoring 15m then close. file a brief incident note with action items.

maya: creating incident note: /ops/incidents/4932106789-canary-flap.md — summary: transient canary-induced 5xx spike, auto-resolved, no customer impact. Actions: lower canary rate, enforce per-route conn limits, add canary-specific retry/backoff, adjust PD rule to require sustained window.

eli: i'll take the watch and follow up with QA to adjust canary load tests.

simon: handing off to eli — i'm offshift in ~25m.

eli: taking watch. ping me if it flaps again. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all — closing thread if stable after 15m.
